measured.source: measured 2026-09-10 by pgrepair (SciPyWeightedILP) on the frozen EUR-Lex truth, three identical runs, journal sha256 in measures/reachability-by-damage-2026-09-10.json. Per damage class, not per form: two forms of the same damage and the same visibility get the same answer.

obstacle.reason: One entity written as two is repaired by MERGING them. Deleting the twin removes the false node and does not give back the facts it took: measured, 24 twins deleted of 1,355 and 1,674 true facts not restored.
obstacle.reason_fr: Une entité écrite en deux se répare en les FUSIONNANT. Supprimer le jumeau retire le faux nœud et ne rend pas les faits qu'il avait emportés : mesuré, 24 jumeaux sur 1 355 et 1 674 faits vrais non rétablis.
obstacle.source: derived from what a deletion-only repair can express, read in the repairer's own code — its solution is a set of elements to delete and carries no insertion — together with the measurement of 2026-09-10. Per damage class, not per form.

history.event: proposed by the Voûte Claude in 'FORMES-PUBMED-pour-Fault-Atlas (09-09-2026)' (part 1; final file sha256 51a338add43cd071…), form 1 of 23; effect on a graph: One biological object (the protein, the target) becomes two to four nodes depending on the species studied; counts and degrees split between them; a blind reunion by surface name would merge orthologues that are not the same entity. Prevalence: seen, not counted globally; 3 species duplicates on 20 places of a gene list (June 2018).

registry_scope.extent: every gene record whose ortholog exists in another species, out of 4,929,431 living genes
registry_scope.why_not_a_prevalence: a fault of a registry has no prevalence: it is a property of the base, so everything drawn from that base carries it. What can be stated is the slice it touches.
